                    ### Question
                    A 56 year old female comes to the ED complaining of moderate right eye pain, headache, and acute onset of blurry vision, which she describes as colored halos around lights. She was watching a movie at home with her husband about an hour ago when the pain began. On physical exam of her right eye, her pupil is mid-dilated and unresponsive to light. Her right eyeball is firm to pressure. Intraocular pressure (IOP) measured with tonometer is elevated at 36mmHg. Which of the following is the most appropriate emergency treatment?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Timolol ophthalmic solution
opb. Epinephrine ophthalmic solution
opc. Laser peripheral iridotomy
opd. Anti-cholinergic ophthalmic solution
ope. NSAID ophthalmic solution

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient presents with symptoms consistent with acute angle-closure glaucoma, including right eye pain, headache, blurry vision with halos, mid-dilated unresponsive pupil, and elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) of 36mmHg. Immediate treatment is critical to prevent vision loss. While timolol ophthalmic solution can lower IOP, it is not a definitive treatment for acute angle-closure glaucoma. The standard emergency treatment is laser peripheral iridotomy, which addresses the underlying cause by creating a new drainage pathway for aqueous humor. This aligns with the consensus that laser peripheral iridotomy is the most effective emergency intervention for this condition.
